subsystems.name: Planetary protection classification and limits
subsystems.role: decides what each mission must do, based on where it goes and what it will do there.

subsystems.name: Cleanliness engineering
subsystems.role: builds and assembles hardware with as few viable microbes and spores as possible.
parts: microbial reduction by dry heat or other means

subsystems.name: Verification and monitoring
subsystems.role: tries to prove that the numbers on paper match the hardware.

subsystems.name: Sample container and seals
subsystems.role: keeps alien material isolated from Earth from the moment it is collected.

subsystems.name: Containment facility
subsystems.role: is where a returned sample is received, opened and worked on without escape.

subsystems.name: Life detection and sample analysis
subsystems.role: asks whether anything in the sample is alive or was ever alive, before distributing it.

buildSteps.title: Assign the mission category
buildSteps.detail: An international body rates the mission — a flyby of a dead world needs little, a Mars lander searching for life needs the most. The rating becomes a hard engineering requirement.

buildSteps.title: Design against contamination
buildSteps.detail: Trajectory analysts bound the chance of an accidental impact on a protected world, while engineers set a bioburden budget for the spacecraft.

buildSteps.title: Build clean
buildSteps.detail: Components are made and mated in cleanrooms, with controlled air, garments and wipe-downs of every surface and tool.

buildSteps.title: Reduce and count microbes
buildSteps.detail: Hardware is baked or otherwise treated to kill spores, then sampled and assayed against the limit before flight.

buildSteps.title: Collect and seal the sample
buildSteps.detail: The sampler fills a container that is sealed inside the landing craft, with witness plates recording what the outside picked up.

buildSteps.title: Commission the containment lab
buildSteps.detail: Before launch, if not before landing, the receiving facility is built and certified: negative pressure, filtered exhaust, sealed gloveboxes, sterilisation routes.

buildSteps.title: Receive and open
buildSteps.detail: The capsule is recovered, taken to the facility and opened inside a glovebox — never in ordinary air.

buildSteps.title: Test, then decide
buildSteps.detail: Preliminary life-detection tests run before anything is released; only then are portions distributed to outside laboratories, under continuing controls.

prerequisites.why: spacecraft assembly already borrows heavily from semiconductor and pharmaceutical clean manufacturing.
heat and other treatments can substantially cut spore counts, though they stress delicate instruments.
maximum-containment labs for dangerous pathogens already provide the pressure, filtration and sealing patterns.
a container must stay leak-tight through launch, years in space and a high-speed Earth entry.
finding a few cells or faint organic signatures in a small sample is at the edge of what instruments can do.
the framework rests on a 1967 treaty obligation, but compliance is largely voluntary and now involves many commercial actors.

pathway.milestone: every robotic mission to a sensitive target carries a protection plan
pathway.unlocks: exploration of Mars, Europa and icy moons without careless contamination.

pathway.milestone: returned asteroid samples already curated in sealed facilities
pathway.unlocks: working practice in receiving, opening and distributing extraterrestrial material.

pathway.milestone: a planned Mars sample return and its purpose-built containment laboratory
pathway.unlocks: the first real test of backward protection against material from a world that may have had life.

pathway.milestone: crewed Mars missions and routine commercial lunar activity
pathway.unlocks: forces the rules to handle humans as contamination sources, and to apply far beyond government space agencies.
